subject: Marketplace listing renewal — risk assessment & mitigation
messages:
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing renewal — risk assessment & mitigation

Team —

FYI: AWS and GCP renewal windows for our marketplace listings fall in Q3. We just received an alert from Marketplace Partners (attached) that AWS intends to roll a revised commission schedule that would increase listing fees for API-first vendors. This directly impacts our unit economics for Hosted API customers.

Ask: can you both help run a quick risk assessment focused on: 
- Incremental cost impact by product line (Hosted API, Dedicated): guesstimate token volume uplift + fee delta
- Negotiation levers (commit discounts, co-sell credits, promotional listing credits) for AWS and GCP
- Contingency playbook: if we can’t move the fees, what are short-term mitigations (pricing guardrails, targeted SKU delisting, amortized credits)

Owner suggestions: Kar, can you own the AWS negotiation strategy and numbers? Marissa, can you own the commercial impact & go-to-market mitigations and draft the exec ask for a fee carve-out / credit? I’ll coordinate cross-functional asks with Finance and Legal.

Deliverables by EOD Jul 8: 1-page risk summary + one-slide recommended mitigation plan so I can route to Execs for approval. I attached the partner note the marketplace sent plus the current listing fee schedule.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: listing_fee_schedule_Q3-2027.pdf
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing renewal — risk assessment & mitigation

Lauren / Marissa —

Thanks — I’ll take point on AWS. Quick notes from my side after a first-pass on the attached schedule: 
- Back-of-envelope: if the proposed fee delta (~+8–12% on listing commission) sticks, our per-API-call contribution margin for Hosted customers drops ~4–6% at current volumes. Biggest hit is for high-throughput embeddings customers.
- Negotiation levers: commit tiers are the quickest win (push for higher commit threshold that includes listing credits), ask for delayed effective date tied to our next quarter bookings, and request a 6–12 month promotional listing credit to smooth the transition.
- Data needed from Sales: Marissa, can you pull top 10 accounts by monthly token spend and flag customers on trials/credits? We should prioritize accounts sensitive to per-token pricing.

I’ll draft the AWS negotiation bullet points and the ask language for Partner Manager outreach. If AWS is rigid we should prioritize asking for co-sell credits or marketing funds to offset the impact.

– Kar
Karthik Iyer
Strategic Partnerships | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Marketplace listing renewal — commission schedule update

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the note and for the heads up. We’re sending the official renewal quote and proposed commission schedule (attached). High-level options we can offer: 

1) Standard renewal: new commission bands effective Aug 1 — discounted incremental tiers apply only after volume thresholds.
2) Commitment-backed credit: sign a 12-month commit (baseline + growth) and receive listing credit that offsets up to 8% of incremental fees.
3) Transitional promo: a 3–6 month promotional credit for eligible new listings or renewed SKUs.

We’re open to structuring a blended solution (option 2 + 3) depending on your forecast and go-to-market activities. Please review the attached aws_renewal_quote_2027.xlsx and confirm a time for a 45-min negotiation call next week; Sophie Martin on my team will attend.

Best,
Sophie Martin

Lauren / Kar —

Attached is the one-page risk summary and the mitigation slide we promised. TL;DR: the most practical path that balances speed and economics is: 

1) Push AWS for a commitment-backed credit (Option 2) calibrated to our 12-month forecast; get legal to accept a limited-duration amendment rather than a full contract redline.
2) Ask GCP for a matching promotional credit for the first 90 days post-renewal — we can time this to a joint marketing push to recover customer impact.
3) Short-term product mitigations: temporarily limit high-throughput public trial tiers and move select large customers to Dedicated where listing fees are amortized across committed capacity.

Next steps I’ve scheduled: 
- Negotiation call with AWS (Sophie Martin) and our Counsel on Jul 20, 10:00am PT — invite pending.
- Internal finance approval request scheduled for Jul 18 EOD (I’ll prep the exec ask doc).
- Marissa will pull top 10 accounts by Jul 16 for prioritized outreach.

If you approve this approach I’ll finalize the ask wording and the slide for Exec review.

Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
